sources.title: Practical tips for improving your broadband speed
facts: The page explains the Broadband Speeds Code of Practice protections.
It notes the broadband universal service obligation right to request a decent connection.
limits: Home troubleshooting does not diagnose provider-network faults.
A right to request service is not proof of immediate availability.

sources.title: Statement: Better Broadband Speeds Information - Voluntary Codes of Practice
facts: The statement strengthened speed information and contract-exit rights.
It describes minimum guaranteed speed information before sign-up.
limits: The statement is regulatory evidence rather than a live speed test.
Individual line performance requires current measurements.

sources.title: Broadband speeds: what you need to know
sources.geo: United Kingdom customers of participating providers
facts: Participating providers must give clear speed information when a service is bought.
Customers may exit without penalty if a network speed problem is not fixed within the code period.
limits: Protections apply only to participating providers and qualifying services.
The guide does not establish the speed at a specific premises.

sources.title: A summary of Ofcom's rules for phone and broadband providers
facts: The page summarises provider duties toward disabled and vulnerable customers.
Examples include priority fault repair, text relay and accessible services.
limits: A summary is not the full General Conditions text.
Whether a specific customer qualifies depends on provider procedures and circumstances.

sources.title: Emergency video relay
sources.geo: United Kingdom deaf British Sign Language users
facts: Emergency video relay lets BSL users contact emergency services.
The service is available 24 hours a day and is free to use.
limits: A connected device and data connection are required.
The page does not measure local broadband availability.

sources.title: Emergency video relay: how it will work
facts: The obligation came into force on 17 June 2022.
Relevant internet-access and number-based communications providers must facilitate access where the rules apply.
limits: The page explains obligations rather than testing provider compliance.
PDF rule text was not parsed.

sources.title: Accessibility
sources.geo: United Kingdom communications users and providers
facts: The index lists accessibility guidance, General Conditions and emergency video relay evaluation records.
It separates consumer advice from industry regulation.
limits: An index is source-lineage evidence only.
Listed records have different dates and purposes.

sources.title: General Conditions of Entitlement
facts: All providers within scope must comply with applicable General Conditions.
The current consolidated conditions referenced by the page came into force on 8 April 2026.
limits: The HTML overview is not a substitute for the full legal instrument.
Applicability varies by provider and condition.

sources.title: Amendments to the General Conditions of Entitlement
facts: The page records superseded consolidated versions and amendment statements.
It records April 2025 changes concerning Global Titles and mobile network security.
limits: Archived versions must not be treated as current rules.
The index does not by itself determine compliance.

sources.title: The Communications Market 2026
facts: The report portal combines industry data, Ofcom consumer research and selected third-party headline figures.
The publication date is 30 June 2026.
limits: Market-level data is aggregate.
The portal does not establish current service at an individual premises.
